newsitem.title: FRANCE: French stocks end lower on profit-taking.
newsitem.headline: French stocks end lower on profit-taking.

text.p: French shares ended lower on profit-taking on Wednesday as investors feared a correction with the market at such high levels, dealers said.

"This downturn is normal. We're at levels where people start getting worried," one trader said. "The market needs to breathe before resuming its upward move. That's why the good U.S. figures didn't really help," said another.
The favourable January inflation data failed also to ignite a rally on Wall Street.
The blue-chip CAC 40 index finished down 22.76 points or 0.87 percent at 2594.76 while the CAC-40 futures contract was down 1.0 points at 2,607.
Volume totalled a robust 8.50 billion francs.

Thomson-CSF climbed 3.7 percent to 182 francs, powered by the French government's plans to sell its 58 percent stake in the defence electronics firm via a private placement. Missiles- to-publishing group Lagardere fell 2.69 percent with dealers saying investors believed engineering giant Alcatel Alsthom would win the battle for Thomson-CSF.
"The market is betting on Alcatel," said one dealer. Alcatel, whose shares had risen in recently on the belief that it is the favourite to take over Thomson-CSF, shed 0.68 percent to 585 francs.

Steelmaker Usinor Sacilor bucked a losing trend, gaining 1.26 percent to 88.30, building on Tuesday's advance after forecasting better 1997 results. Its 1996 profits slid to 1.49 billion francs from 4.43 billion the previous year.

Accor rose 0.52 percent to 768 francs. After gaining on 1996 sales figures, the shares erased part of their advance when Generale de Belgique, a unit of Cie de Suez, said it was selling shares in in the hotel group for a capital gain of over two billion Belgian francs. Fund managers said SGB sold its eight percent stake for 756 francs per share.
